newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria seeks credits to buy crude oil.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria seeks credits to buy crude oil.

text.p: Bulgaria's biggest oil refinery, Neftohim, struggling with a shortage of cash and crude, has agreed a credit with France's Paribas bank branch in Geneva, a refinery spokeswoman said on Tuesday.
Tatyana Hadzhieva said Neftohim's finance director Atanas Zaikov had signed an agreement in Geneva to open a credit line funding the refinery's purchase of crude.
She said the volume of the credit was a commercial secret.

However, another plant official, who declined to be named said the credit would not solve Neftohim's inability to pay its crude suppliers or settle its huge debts to suppliers who refuse further crude deliveries to the plant.
"We need credits for crude supplies until the end of the year," he said.
Russia's state-owned Rosneft oil company said last week it had reduced crude oil supplies to Neftohim because of unpaid debts.
On Tuesday Neftohim increased refined daily oil volumes to 8,500 tonnes from 6,500 tonnes but they are still near the critical minimum, Hadzhieva said.

Neftohim, which continues to distribute limited volumes of up to 1,000 tonnes of petrol per day for the domestic market, expects a tanker of 66,300 tonnes of Russian crude of private firm Yucos Petroleum Bulgaria to arrive in the Black Sea port of Bourgas on Wednesday.
"Three more tankers have been agreed to arrive by the end of February," Hadzhieva said.
Neftohim officials say regular government revisions of fuel prices have not kept up with a recent drastic fall of the lev against the dollar. A litre of gasoline now costs 10-14 cents.
